svg.text: How a file of unknown shape becomes a grounded, cited answer — and where the tenant boundary sits at every step.
Solid = built. Dashed = designed, not built. Red = the isolation boundary.
1 · INGESTION — format, meaning, and trust are three separate jobs
Format is the easy part — a reader swap. Meaning is the hard part. Today ingest_minitab.py knows CEMEX's column names, units, timezone and
baseline policy in 124 lines of Python; customer #2 means a second file exactly like it. A profile is data, so it can be diffed, reviewed by a
metallurgist, and REPLAYED when a mapping turns out wrong. A loader is code — it can only be rewritten.
every number traces to a file, an upload,
a person, and a mapping version
2 · WHERE DATA LIVES — three planes, one boundary
TENANT PLANE one database per customer
isolated · separately backed up · DROP DATABASE = deletion
→ which is why its harness differs
abstractions only — never a customer's rows
evidence_signatures how it LOOKS in data
discriminators how to tell it from lookalikes
Confirmed 23× across 6 sites. Discriminator: F10 unchanged."
3 · RETRIEVAL — three modes, chosen by question shape (this is what "RAG" means here)
Do NOT embed the time series. "Outliers in the last 3 hours" is a WHERE clause — nearest-neighbour returns semantically nearby rows, which has no
relationship to CORRECT rows. The wrong count arrives sounding exactly like a right one. Structured pre-filter first; vectors are the fallback.
4 · CONTEXT WINDOW — assembled by code, never chosen by the model
TARGET ~15k input · hard ceiling 25k · max 8 tool calls · per-tenant daily cost ceiling
A 200k context window is a budget, not a target. Compute statistics in Python — never make the model do arithmetic.
